column3: “Late of the Sabbaths” is rendered “after the Sabbath”; “tomb” is rendered “grave.”
“A great earthquake” is rendered “a severe earthquake had occurred”; NASB has no “from the door,” like the critical text.
NASB follows the critical text: “where He was lying,” without “the Lord.”
NASB follows the critical text without the Textus Receptus clause “as they went to tell His disciples”; “saying, Greetings” is rendered “greeted them.”
NASB renders “brothers” as “brethren” and adds “take word.”
NASB renders “silver pieces many” as “a large sum of money.”
“Be heard by the governor” is rendered “come to the governor’s ears,” and “persuade” is “win him over.”
NASB has no “to Him,” like the critical text; “doubted” is rendered “were doubtful.”
NASB follows the critical text without “Amen”; “all the days” is rendered “always,” and “completion” is “end.”
